What is Ondo (ONDO)?

Ondo specialises in tokenising real-world assets (RWAs), such as US Treasury bonds and other fixed-income instruments, making them accessible in a decentralised and liquid marketplace.
Note
Luno does not currently support sending or receiving ONDO, but you can still buy or sell it like any of our other cryptocurrencies. This decision has been made in order to ensure there are appropriate controls in place to maintain the highest standards of investor protection. Learn more about why you can't send or receive ONDO.
Who created Ondo?
Ondo Finance was founded in 2021 by Nathan Allman and Pinku Surana, who both formerly worked at Goldman Sachs. Recognising inefficiencies in traditional markets, they launched Ondo to bring institutional-grade financial products onto the blockchain, making them more accessible, liquid, and transparent.
Since its inception, Ondo Finance has grown rapidly, securing partnerships with major financial players, including Mastercard, which integrates Ondo’s tokenised assets into its Multi-Token Network (MTN). The company continues to expand its ecosystem, offering new ways for institutions and individuals to interact with real-world assets in a decentralised environment.
How does Ondo work?
Ondo enables you to tokenise real-world assets (RWAs) and offer them as blockchain-based financial products. The company’s ecosystem is built on Ondo Chain, a proof-of-stake Layer 1 blockchain specifically designed for institutional-grade assets. Its infrastructure allows investors to securely buy, trade, and manage tokenised assets while ensuring compliance with financial regulations.
Through its platform, users can participate in various investment strategies, such as liquidity provisioning, stablecoin yield farming, and volatility trading. Ondo also integrates Chainlink oracles to provide real-time pricing data, ensuring accurate and efficient execution of these financial instruments.
The flagship product, OUSG (Short-Term US Government Treasuries Fund), enables qualified investors to hold US Treasuries in a tokenised format, providing liquidity and accessibility that traditional markets lack. Investors can mint and redeem their tokenised assets 24/7, bypassing the operational restrictions of traditional finance.
What is the native cryptocurrency of Ondo?
Ondo Chain’s native cryptocurrency is ONDO. ONDO plays a central role within the ecosystem, facilitating governance, rewards, and incentivising liquidity providers. As part of Ondo's decentralised model, ONDO holders have the power to participate in governance decisions, such as voting on proposals that affect the future direction of the platform, new product offerings, and strategic developments. This ensures that the community has a say in how the ecosystem evolves.
In addition to governance, ONDO is also used to reward participants in the ecosystem. For example, liquidity providers earn ONDO as compensation for contributing capital to various investment pools. The token is designed to foster active engagement within the ecosystem, ensuring that stakeholders are incentivised to support the platform’s growth.
Moreover, ONDO tokens are used to pay for transaction fees within the system, ensuring the platform remains secure and operational.

What is Ondo (ONDO)?
Published: Feb 4, 2025
Table of Contents
Ondo Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform that bridges the gap between traditional finance (TradFi) and blockchain technology by tokenizing real-world assets (RWAs). By bringing institutional-grade financial products onto the blockchain, Ondo aims to create a more accessible, transparent, and efficient financial ecosystem.
The History of Ondo
Ondo Finance was founded to make institutional-grade financial products accessible to everyone. Traditionally, these opportunities were limited to banks, hedge funds, and accredited investors. By leveraging blockchain technology, Ondo is breaking down these barriers and bringing real-world assets (RWAs) into the DeFi space.
To achieve this, Ondo has:

Partnered with institutional asset managers to enable the tokenization of RWAs.
Launched Ondo DAO, giving governance power to the community.
Expanded access to institutional DeFi, attracting both crypto and traditional finance investors.

Ondo Features
Tokenization of Real-World Assets (RWAs)
Ondo converts bonds, funds, and securities into digital tokens, making them easier to trade, more transparent, and accessible to a wider range of investors.
Blockchain as Middleware
Ondo acts as a bridge between TradFi and DeFi, ensuring seamless integration, security through smart contracts, and regulatory compliance for institutional adoption.
Institutional-Grade Financial Products
Unlike crypto assets, Ondo offers regulated investment options like:

USDY – A stablecoin yield product with predictable returns.
OUSG – A tokenized fund backed by BlackRock, offering institutional-grade exposure.

Governance & Decentralization
The ONDO token gives holders voting power over protocol fees, smart contract updates, and DAO governance, ensuring the community shapes Ondo’s future.
ONDO: The Token
The ONDO token serves as both the governance and utility token within the Ondo ecosystem. As a governance token, ONDO holders can vote on key protocol changes, including economic policies, feature upgrades, and smart contract improvements. This ensures that the community has a voice in shaping the future of Ondo Finance.
Beyond governance, ONDO also helps oversee Flux Finance and the Ondo DAO, maintaining a decentralized and adaptive ecosystem. While ONDO does not represent ownership of any underlying financial assets, it grants holders the ability to influence protocol decisions.

What Is Ondo Finance (ONDO)?

September 20, 2024
6 min read


Cryptocurrency has evolved rapidly, bringing decentralized finance (DeFi) and tokenized assets to the forefront of financial markets. Amid this transformative era, Ondo Finance has gained significant attention as a protocol aiming to fill the gap between conventional finance and the emerging world of DeFi. In a story akin to the internet’s financial revolution’s early days, Ondo Finance offers innovative solutions that make real-world assets (RWA) accessible to a broad spectrum of investors.
For those familiar with cryptocurrency, you might recall the initial rise of decentralized finance as a major turning point in how we interact with money and investments. Similarly, Ondo Finance is playing a pivotal role today by offering liquidity services and tokenized assets with the aim of making real-world investments more accessible. This article by Argoox will delve deep into the operations of Ondo Finance (ONDO) and how it fits into the broader cryptocurrency landscape.
What is The Definition of Ondo Finance (ONDO)?
Ondo Finance is a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform that allows users to access structured financial products, particularly focused on bringing real-world assets into the decentralized ecosystem. O NDO is the native governance token of the platform, used to vote on important decisions and stake in return for rewards. By using a decentralized model, Ondo facilitates new investment opportunities by providing liquidity to traditional financial assets, such as bonds and real estate, while leveraging the benefits of blockchain technology.
Who Are the Founders of Ondo Finance?
Ondo Finance was founded by former Goldman Sachs employees, drawing from deep expertise in both traditional finance and decentralized technologies. Nate Hindman, former head of growth at Bancor, and Amnon Samid, a recognized figure in the blockchain space, are key leaders behind this ambitious project. The experience of the founding team gives the platform an edge in understanding both the conventional financial markets and the decentralized finance ecosystem, which is reflected in their business model.
What Does Ondo Finance (ONDO) Do in Crypto?
Ondo Finance provides a platform that specializes in structured finance for decentralized assets. Essentially, Ondo allows for the tokenization of real-world assets, enabling investors to buy shares of these assets through blockchain. For example, investors can participate in bond markets, real estate, and other traditional asset classes while benefiting from DeFi’s transparency, efficiency, and low costs. Ondo’s unique proposition is its focus on bridging decentralized finance with the broader, traditional financial markets through innovative solutions like liquidity provisioning and yield management.
Is Ondo Finance Legit?
Yes, Ondo Finance is considered legitimate in the cryptocurrency space, having raised significant capital from prominent venture capital firms. Furthermore, Ondo Finance’s collaborations with reputable institutional partners, such as investment giant BlackRock, solidify its status as a serious player in the crypto world. The platform’s commitment to security and transparency, as well as its real-world use cases, underscores its credibility.
Read More: What is Ondo (ONDO) Trading Bot?
What Blockchain Is Ondo Finance On?
Ondo Finance operates primarily on the Ethereum blockchain, which is the most widely used decentralized network for DeFi applications. By leveraging Ethereum’s smart contract technology, Ondo ensures that all transactions are clear, secure, and immutable. Ethereum’s robust infrastructure also allows Ondo to scale and integrate with other DeFi applications, expanding its user base and increasing the utility of its ONDO token.
What Makes Ondo Finance (ONDO) Unique?
Ondo Finance stands out by focusing on real-world assets (RWAs) and enabling institutional-grade liquidity. While many DeFi platforms offer staking or yield farming primarily on digital assets, Ondo goes a step further by incorporating real-world financial products into its ecosystem. This creates a broader range of investment opportunities, especially for traditional investors who are new to cryptocurrency. Its dual focus on decentralized governance and real-world utility makes Ondo unique in the DeFi space.
Is Ondo Finance (ONDO) Decentralized?
Yes, Ondo Finance operates as a decentralized autonomous organization (DAO), meaning decisions about the platform are made through community voting, typically involving ONDO token holders. This decentralized governance model ensures that no single entity controls the protocol, aligning with the core ethos of DeFi and giving power to the community to shape the future of the platform.
How Many ONDO Coins Are There in Circulation?
As of now, there are approximately 100 million ONDO tokens in circulation, with a total supply of 1 billion tokens. A portion of these tokens is allocated for governance, rewards, and future ecosystem development. The circulating supply can impact the price and availability of ONDO on various exchanges, making it an important metric for investors to follow.
Where Can You Buy ONDO?
ONDO tokens can be purchased on several major cryptocurrency exchanges, including decentralized platforms like Uniswap, as well as centralized exchanges that list the tokens. Additionally, Ondo’s own platform allows users to interact with the token directly for governance and liquidity purposes. Always ensure that you use trusted exchanges and wallets when buying ONDO.
Where Is Ondo Finance Located?
Ondo Finance is a decentralized protocol and does not have a central physical location. However, the team behind the project is based primarily in the United States, with contributors and developers spread across the globe. The protocol itself is governed by its community through decentralized governance mechanisms.
What Is Ondo Finance RWA?
Ondo Finance’s RWA (Real-World Assets) program is a major component of its business model. This initiative focuses on tokenizing traditional assets like real estate, bonds, and commodities, making them more accessible to DeFi users. By bridging the gap between real-world investments and blockchain technology, Ondo opens up new avenues for investors to divide their portfolios while enjoying the benefits of decentralization.
Is Ondo Finance Backed by BlackRock?
Yes, Ondo Finance has established a partnership with BlackRock. It’s one of the world’s largest asset management firms. Moreover, this collaboration aims to bring institutional-grade liquidity and traditional financial assets into the decentralized finance space. The partnership with BlackRock is a significant vote of confidence in Ondo Finance’s vision and adds a layer of legitimacy to the platform’s offerings.

Conclusion
Ondo Finance (ONDO) represents a promising step forward in the evolution of decentralized finance. Because of bridging capability to fill the gap of real-world assets and the DeFi ecosystem, Ondo offers investors new opportunities to engage with traditional financial products in a decentralized manner. Also, with strong partnerships, including BlackRock, a robust governance model, and a focus on real-world utility, Ondo Finance is uniquely positioned to shape the future of finance.
For those looking to explore decentralized finance with a focus on real-world assets, Ondo Finance presents a compelling option. Overview
Stakeholders in the DAO — ONDO token holders — exercise control over the protocol, including economic parameters and smart contract upgrades, through on-chain governance proposals.
The DAO might also elect committees or multisigs to manage certain processes, such as updating certain economic parameters or pausing the protocol in critical times.
Governance Process
The governance process will typically follow a two-stage process: a forum discussion and an on-chain vote.
Governance proposals will typically start with a post on the Flux Finance Governance Forum (opens in a new tab). The post, though optional, is strongly encouraged. Feedback from the community and team will materially increase the chances of a successful and well-aligned governance proposal. Anyone can post and contribute to the discussion on the forum.
Once the governance proposal is finalized, you can submit a proposal for a binding on-chain vote. The DAO is a fork of Compound's Governor Bravo (opens in a new tab) and uses Tally to manage the on-chain voting process. Voting power is based on ONDO token ownership, and token holders can delegate their voting power to other wallets.
The DAO parameters are set as follows:

Proposal Threshold: 100,000,000 ONDO
To submit a proposal, you need to have this much voting power (directly and/or delegated to you). This rule is necessary to reduce spam or malicious proposals.


Voting Period: 3 days
Once the voting period is live, people will be able to cast votes during this period, after which the proposal becomes binding and can be executed.


Quorum: 1,000,000 ONDO
Proposals will only pass if there is enough voting power to pass the quorum.


Timelock: 1 day
Successful proposals will execute after this delay period once the voting period completes.
